observations: Three photos show a black metal bunk bed frame outdoors on a paved surface.
The frame has two levels with horizontal slats for mattress support.
The structure includes vertical posts, side rails, and a ladder on one side.
The top bunk has a guardrail on the side facing the ladder and a handrail at the head.
The paint appears to be intact but shows minor scuffs and wear, especially on the vertical posts.
No mattresses or bedding are present.
The background includes a road with trucks and a building with a yellow wall in photo 1 and 2.
Watermarks 'POSTED ON JI GOOKAMP' are visible on all photos.

claims.claim: Tired of bunk beds that sway like a palm tree? Stop risking your safety on shaky frames!
claims.evidence: The stability of the frame cannot be assessed from still photos; no movement or load test is shown.

risks.risk: The frame may be unstable or wobbly under use, especially on the top bunk.
risks.proof: A video showing the frame being shaken or a person standing on the top bunk to test stability.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially unstable, which reduces value

risks.risk: Hidden rust or structural damage not visible in photos, especially at joints or welds.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all joints, welds, and base connections, especially under the bed and at the ladder attachment points.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly compromised, which reduces value

risks.risk: The frame may be missing parts or have loose bolts, which could affect safety.
risks.proof: A photo showing all bolts and fasteners, especially at the corners and ladder connections, to confirm they are tight and present.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly incomplete or loose, which reduces value

proof_requests: Video of the frame being shaken or a person standing on the top bunk to test stability.
Close-up photos of all joints, welds, and base connections.
Photo showing all bolts and fasteners to confirm they are tight and present.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a bunk bed frame, but critical risks related to stability, structural integrity, and completeness cannot be assessed from the current photos. These risks directly affect safety and value, so proof is required before pricing.
